territorial_scope.description: Applies to data centers in the State of New Jersey.

evidence.quote: the owner or operator of a data center in the State shall prepare and submit a water and energy usage report

summary.short: Bill S3379 (second reprint) would require owners and operators of New Jersey data centers to submit semi-annual water and energy usage reports to the Board of Public Utilities. The Board would publish basic and usage information online; performance and sustainability data from facilities receiving State financial incentives would be confidential.
summary.long: The bill (S3379, second reprint) would add a section to Title 48 on water and energy usage at data centers. Data centers are facilities primarily providing digital data storage and processing, with a carve-out for health care providers' internal operations. Owners and operators would submit a water and energy usage report to the Board of Public Utilities within six months of the effective date (three months for facilities operating a year or more), then semi-annually. Reports cover facility details, energy and water use, the serving electric utility, on-site power supplies and water sources. Facilities receiving State financial incentives must also report efficiency and sustainability indicators. The Board would publish basic and usage reports within 30 days; performance and sustainability information stays confidential, except anonymized aggregates from at least five facilities. Substantial changes require notice 60 days in advance. Reporting runs three years from a facility's first submission, after which the Board decides whether to make it permanent. The act takes effect immediately.

relations.note: Savings clause: section 1 does not abridge, alter or amend State agency disclosure obligations under this act, and the Board's disclosure obligations for information not submitted under subsection c are preserved.

relations.target_text: P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.), Open Public Records Act
relations.note: Information submitted under subsection c is confidential and not subject to disclosure under that act or the common law right of access; subsection d(2) preserves other disclosure obligations.

relations.target_text: P.L.1968, c.410 (C.52:14B-1 et seq.), Administrative Procedure Act
relations.note: If the Board makes the reporting requirement permanent, it must adopt rules and regulations to implement the section in accordance with that act.
The act is stated to supplement Title 48; the text does not give codified section numbers.

notes: The document is the Second Reprint of a bill (S3379, current version as reported by the Assembly committee on June 4, 2026, with amendments), not an enacted text; the registry's in_force and adopted status is not shown in the document. Reprint markers (superscript-numbered insertions and bracketed deletions) are present in the text and are not separately coded. Sec. 1.f says the reporting requirement applies for three years from the date a data center first submits a report, regardless of commencement or the effective date, while Sec. 1.b sets first-report deadlines from the effective date; it is unclear whether the three-year period runs per facility or for the requirement as a whole. Relation target_instrument_id values are left empty because the cited acts were not verified against the registry.
